## 2c904a701029

### Finding 1 — declared override axes are no-ops, and unknown overrides are accepted

The generator declares eight axes, but several are never consumed through `GenCtx`: `palette_size` is chosen with `rng.randint`, while `palette_kind`, `position_bias`, `n_distinct_colors`, and `density` do not affect construction. There is also no explicit unknown-override check.

Concrete probe: with seed 17, sample 3, difficulty `medium`, the baseline grid was byte-identical after each of these calls:

```text
palette_size=2
palette_size=5
palette_kind=warm
palette_kind=cool
position_bias=concentric_5_frames
n_distinct_colors=6
density=balanced
texture=warm
texture=cool
made_up_axis=123
```

Every call was accepted, including the undeclared `made_up_axis`. This makes exact curriculum controls untrustworthy and lets orchestration believe it requested a branch that was never realized.

### Finding 2 — `self_check` accepts merged frames that the Racket rule no longer treats as separate depths

For the generated seed-17/sample-3 medium grid, changing only cell `(3,1)` from `0` to `5` bridges the outer and inner frame. The number of 4-connected color-5 body components drops from two to one, yet `self_check` still returns `[]` because it checks ring boundaries but does not reject extra bridge cells or verify component separation.

The canonical rule obtains frames from `(objects body 0)`. On the bridged board there is one merged color-5 object, so the rule cannot recolor two independent depth frames even though the checker claims the scene contains at least two. The checker should validate exact frame components, reject off-frame color-5 cells, and ensure the observed frame count matches the requested `n_frames`.
